solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cautious holding sides of table that's weak

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two end letters, so only T and E of 'table' are used
the word for cautious holds the table's sides inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of TABLE

explanation.surface: Someone nervously guarding a flimsy piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weak' here is weak as in thin tea or soup, which is why WATERY fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery drinks or broths are weak, diluted ones.

clue.text: Untiring don is penning article in French

indicators.note: 'is' penning something writes it inside IS

blocks.note: to don clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: A tireless university lecturer busy writing an article in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like the Oxbridge lecturer, noun, but it is the verb to put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Weariless means never growing weary, so untiring.

clue.text: The crane almost shifted block

indicators.note: almost the crane is the crane without its last letter
the letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A building-site crane has nearly moved a heavy block into place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a block of stone; a tranche is a block of shares or money instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from finance: a block of shares or a slice of funding released in one go is called a tranche.

clue.text: Fondly recall bizarre mini scent bottles

indicators.note: the phrase bottles the answer, holding it inside

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word, through the second, into the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a collection of odd little perfume bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' reads as a noun, perfume bottles, but it is the verb that holds the answer inside: bizar(RE MINI SCE)nt.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, and the adverb matters: reminiscing is remembering with pleasure, not just remembering.

clue.text: Garment deliveries by company essentially late

indicators.note: the essence of 'late' is its middle, AT

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries
the middle two letters of LATE

explanation.surface: A courier firm's clothing parcels keep arriving late.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the bowler delivers the ball six times in an over, so 'deliveries' can stand for OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcoat is a garment worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Plonk duck in Indian river after struggling

indicators.note: the letters struggle out of their order

blocks.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A duck floundering in an Indian river.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck is not a bird but a cricket score of zero, O. Plonk is British slang for cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin ordinaire is cheap everyday table wine, which is what plonk means.

clue.text: Regret accepting opening in Labour government

indicators.note: the opening of Labour is its first letter
the word for regret accepts a letter inside it

explanation.surface: A politician regrets taking a job in a Labour government.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is British party politics, but 'Labour government' splits: 'Labour' feeds the letter and 'government' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the act of governing: a period under one party is its rule, as in years of Tory rule.

clue.text: Dim bishop entering wrong course

indicators.note: a wrong course has its letters in the wrong order
the bishop enters the rearranged word

explanation.surface: A dim-witted bishop taking the wrong path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' looks like it describes the bishop as stupid; it is the definition, meaning faint or unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure and dim both mean faint or hard to make out.

clue.text: Royal once died in revolutionary defeat

indicators.note: a revolution turns the word round
the letter for died goes in the reversed word

blocks.note: a rout is a heavy defeat
d. = died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A king or queen who once died after being beaten by revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary defeat' suggests a revolt, but 'revolutionary' only turns ROUT around.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors, Henry VIII and Elizabeth I among them, were an English royal house of the past.

clue.text: Warnings when holding large weapon

indicators.note: the word for when holds the other letters inside it

blocks.note: as = when, as in 'as I left'
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: Warnings raised when someone is seen carrying a large weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: ARM as a weapon is the singular of 'arms'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bell or siren that signals danger is an alarm, so the plural matches the plural.

clue.text: Confined near back walls

indicators.note: the back walls in the word for near, surrounding it

blocks.note: the back of something is its end

explanation.surface: Someone confined near the back walls of a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walls' is a verb here: the word for back walls in, surrounding, the word for near.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both past participles: a field fenced round or an animal penned in is shut within limits.

clue.text: Critical inspector put on exhaust testing

blocks.note: to sap is to exhaust, drain of strength
proving = testing, as in the proving ground

explanation.surface: A fault-finding inspector puts a car on an exhaust test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' means put next to, so the pieces sit one after another; 'exhaust' is a verb, not a car part.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both adjectives: a disapproving look is a critical one, expressing an unfavourable judgement.

clue.text: Stirring up trouble in church with new record of past events

blocks.note: a diary records what has happened

explanation.surface: A church troublemaker stirring things up with a fresh history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble in church' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'trouble' and 'in' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Incendiary remarks stir up trouble, figuratively setting things alight.

clue.text: Turning out of bed Right Reverend makes contented sound

indicators.note: turning the word round reverses it

explanation.surface: A bishop turning out of bed in the morning and humming happily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right Reverend' is the formal title of an Anglican bishop, abbreviated RR.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the low rumble a cat makes when it is happy.

clue.text: Heard tune before

indicators.note: the answer is what we hear when the word for tune is spoken

explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'air' and 'ere' sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or poetic synonym, as in 'ere long', meaning before long.

clue.text: They keep one steady as blister is plastered

indicators.note: plastered means drunk, and the drunk letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A child learning to ride a bike needs stabilisers while a blister gets a plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' looks like the blister getting a plaster, but it is slang for drunk. Stabilisers are the small side wheels on a child's bicycle (training wheels).
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the side wheels on a learner's bicycle, or fins on a ship, stop it tipping over.

clue.text: Stiff tail since barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, and mad letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dog's tail has been rigid ever since it started barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' fits the dog picture, but in British slang barking (mad) means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a material with no give, that will not spring or stretch, is rigid.

clue.text: Retreat from scary aunt going berserk

indicators.note: letters going berserk run wild out of order

explanation.surface: Fleeing from a frightening aunt who has lost her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' reads as a verb, to flee, but it is the noun: a place of refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctuary is a retreat, a safe place to withdraw to.

clue.text: Climber on rocks concerning - source of many a drama

indicators.note: in an across clue, the climber sitting on the rocks goes after them, so PEA comes second

blocks.note: the pea is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A mountaineer on rocks has a dramatic story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' is a plant, not a mountaineer, and 'rocks' is a verb, not the cliff face.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote dozens of plays, so he is the source of many a drama.

clue.text: A dull foreign currency enthusiast

blocks.note: EUR is the code for the euro

explanation.surface: A boring foreign-money buff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull' means non-shiny, as in a mat finish, not boring.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something out of love for it, an enthusiast rather than a professional.

clue.text: Child star in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the sound is what counts

explanation.surface: A child actor starring on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child star' looks like one phrase, a young performer, but 'star' begins the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a male offspring is one kind of child.

clue.text: One turns round errant person holding power

indicators.note: the errant person holds the letter for power inside

explanation.surface: Someone turning round on a wrongdoer who has seized power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One turns round' looks like a reversal instruction, but it is the definition: a spinner, or a spin bowler's ball, turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinner is anything that spins, turning round.

clue.text: Decline following prisoner

blocks.note: f. = following, as in page references
an old lag is a long-serving prisoner

explanation.surface: A drop-off after a prisoner's release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' for a prisoner is British slang, as in old lag.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to decline or tire, as energy flags.

clue.text: Expressions right to be censored from comedies

indicators.note: censoring cuts something out, here the R

explanation.surface: Censors cutting phrases out of comedy scripts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expressions' looks like phrases in a script; it means facial expressions.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the facial sense: pulling a face means making an expression.

clue.text: Reporter Jack introducing our northern top celebs

blocks.note: the A-list are the top celebrities

explanation.surface: A reporter named Jack introducing the north's biggest stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like the reporter's name; it is only the card letter J, placed before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who writes news for a paper or broadcaster.

clue.text: Leave queen, one of four in card pack but not spades

indicators.note: 'but not spades' removes the S

blocks.note: Q = queen in cards and chess

blocks.clueFragment: one of four in card pack

explanation.surface: A card player drops the queen while sorting a pack.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is card-playing, so 'queen' looks like part of the pack rather than a lone letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: quitting a job or a house means walking away from it.

clue.text: Lovely birch cue damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A fine snooker cue made of birch has been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovely' seems to praise the cue, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubic means angelic in looks, sweet and lovely like a cherub.

clue.text: At regular points, fanzine art is all around section of lines

indicators.note: taking letters at regular points means every other one
turning the letters all around reverses them

explanation.surface: Fan-magazine art spread around a page of poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' belongs to the fodder, not the grammar, which is why the phrase reads so smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a section of a poem.

clue.text: Acquire backing in casual plan

indicators.note: backing sends the word backwards
the reversed word goes in the word for casual

blocks.note: stray = casual, occasional, as in a stray remark

explanation.surface: Getting financial backing for a relaxed business plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like funding for the plan; it only turns GET around.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a worked-out scheme for reaching a goal, as in a business or battle plan.

clue.text: Beetle in South Asian dish

blocks.note: curry is a South Asian dish

explanation.surface: A beetle found in a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' is a verb here: to beetle off is British for to hurry away.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional (British) verb sense: to beetle along is to hurry with short quick steps, like the insect.
